<reason>Both sides were sharp, disciplined, and correctly used the A1:/A2: structure. PRO built a clean window-of-opportunity case (weak proxies, degraded defenses, rising nuclear trajectory) and landed two real hits: that Fordow and Natanz were exposed by intelligence rather than inspectors, and that an unexecuted red line was leverage evaporating rather than leverage conserved. But CON won the decisive axis. Its reframe of monitoring's value — accounting does not have to find the hidden room, it has to make the hidden room necessary, forcing a covert effort to be a whole second, procurement-visible program — squarely answered PRO's best pressure question instead of dodging it, and reinforced the loss-of-sight cost across the decade-long ledger CON set as the burden in its opening. CON also converted PRO's own concessions: PRO admitted it cannot locate the 60 percent stockpile and shrugged that buried-or-warehoused is "in both cases" fine, which CON then used to puncture the deterrence-restored story ("you cannot credibly threaten an address you cannot name"), and PRO's admission that Iran refrained from dashing because facilities were known and reachable was turned into evidence that the pre-strike posture was already coercing for free. PRO's answer that residual intelligence and procurement signatures suffice was plausible but never resolved why those tools improve after inspectors leave and a struck regime hardens. CON's technical point that 60-to-90 is the small, hideable step also went only partially answered. PRO's clipped opening and clipped second rebuttal are a modest additional execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's answer to PRO's Q2 — "monitoring never had to find the hidden room; it had to make the hidden room necessary," so counted material forces a costly, signature-rich second program while uncounted material forces nothing — combined with the turn on PRO's own concession that it cannot locate the stockpile, which undercut PRO's "detectable and strikeable" forward-looking deterrence claim.</best_rebuttal>
